item.title: The Origin of Physics
item.description:
Physics began as the study of nature: motion, matter, light, and the patterns of the heavens. Its name comes from the Greek physis, meaning “nature.” Ancient civilizations developed practical knowledge of astronomy, mechanics, and measurement, while Greek thinkers sought explanations based on natural causes. Over centuries, scholars across the Islamic world, Asia, and Europe advanced astronomy, optics, and mechanics. The scientific revolution of the sixteenth and seventeenth centuries brought mathematical models, systematic observation, and controlled experiments into closer partnership. Physics later expanded through thermodynamics, electromagnetism, relativity, and quantum mechanics. Equations such as Einstein’s

revealed connections that earlier thinkers could scarcely have imagined—in this case, between mass and energy. From its origins in natural philosophy, physics developed into a discipline in which mathematical explanations must continually answer to observation and experiment.
